section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > ABSTRACT
text: In this work, we develop a novel safranine (SA)-based acidic sulfate copper electronic plating process for through-hole copper void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection, and both the molecule actions and synergistic effects of safranine (SA) are carefully explored. Cyclic voltammetry experiments at rotating rates of 200 r/min and 1200 r/min demonstrate that SA itself can accelerate the electro-reduction of copper ion, heighten the inhibiting effect of polyethylene glycol (PEG) and acceleration effect of bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS).

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > ABSTRACT
text: Cyclic voltammetry experiments at rotating rates of 200 r/min and 1200 r/min demonstrate that SA itself can accelerate the electro-reduction of copper ion, heighten the inhibiting effect of polyethylene glycol (PEG) and acceleration effect of bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS). The addition of SA to the virgin make-up solution (VMS) containing PEG and SPS makes the relative electric charge (ΔQ) between the low and high rotating rates be increased from 1.27 ± 0.04–22.53% ± 0.05, indicating the higher copper electronic plating amount at the center than that at the mouth of through-hole.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > ABSTRACT
text: The addition of SA to the virgin make-up solution (VMS) containing PEG and SPS makes the relative electric charge (ΔQ) between the low and high rotating rates be increased from 1.27 ± 0.04–22.53% ± 0.05, indicating the higher copper electronic plating amount at the center than that at the mouth of through-hole. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy together with theoretical calculations further illustrate that the molecule SA is adsorbed on the copper surface through the N atom in the aromatic ring, PEG and SPS can heighten the adsorption of SA on the Cu surface, and both PEG and SPS both synergistically influence with SA to achieve the void-free copper filling of through-hole.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 1. Introduction
text: With the rapid development of electronic products, advanced fabrication technologies for high-density interconnect (HDI) in the printed circuit board (PCB) are widely applied in 5 G communication, energy devices, wearable devices, and other booming fields [1–3]. Metallization of through-hole (TH) is one of the core technologies to realize the conduction of different layers in HDI-PCB [4,5]. Acidic sulfate copper electronic plating is the most universal process for the metallization of TH [6–9].

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 1. Introduction
text: Acidic sulfate copper electronic plating is the most universal process for the metallization of TH [6–9]. TH copper thickening combined with resin plugging and TH void-free copper filling are the two common metallization technologies. For the TH copper thickening combined with resin plugging technology, only a homogeneous and conformal copper coating (about 20 µm) on its side wall is needed [10–14], then epoxy resin is used to fill the TH. For the TH void-free copper filling technology, copper coating is fully filled inside the TH without any void.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 1. Introduction
text: For the TH void-free copper filling technology, copper coating is fully filled inside the TH without any void. It is worth noting that TH may crack under long-term heating due to the different thermal expansion coeffi cient between the resin and copper, resulting in the blocked signal transmission. Therefore, compared with TH copper thickening combined with resin plugging technology, TH void-free copper filling technology behaves the advantages of higher reliability and better signal transmission quality.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 1. Introduction
text: Nowadays, with the acceleration of communication speed, more heat is generated when the signal processing, the copper void-free filling of TH has therefore been widely employed for improving the heat dissipation efficiency. The main difficulty in copper filling is the formation of voids in TH with higher aspect ratio due to the uneven local current distribution and tanglesome convection environments caused by the specific geometry of TH [15–17]. The copper deposition amount at the mouth is usually higher than that at the center of TH, resulting in the coating in a void or seam.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 1. Introduction
text: The copper deposition amount at the mouth is usually higher than that at the center of TH, resulting in the coating in a void or seam. Therefore, it is particularly crucial introducing the organic additives in the acidic sulfate bath to modulate the copper deposition process at the mouth and center. The key to blind hole filling is the bottom-up growth of copper coating. The key to TH filling is that copper coating rapidly deposits at the center of TH wall until the center is connected to form a butterfly shape structure (two blind holes), and then the two blind holes are filled separately.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 1. Introduction
text: The key to TH filling is that copper coating rapidly deposits at the center of TH wall until the center is connected to form a butterfly shape structure (two blind holes), and then the two blind holes are filled separately. The accelerator of bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS) and suppressor of polyethylene glycol (PEG) are the commonly used additives in the acidic sulfate bath [18–25]. Suppressor, mainly distributed at the mouth of TH, inhibits the copper ion electro-reduction at a definite potential which results in the decrease of reduction current density.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 1. Introduction
text: In this work, we successfully develop a novel and excellent SA-based acidic sulfate copper electronic plating process (additives: PEG, SPS and SA) for the void-free filling of X-shape TH (conducive to the formation of butterfly structure for void-free filling). The intrinsic properties of SA and the interactions among SA, PEG and SPS at the molecule level are expounded through cyclic voltammetry, in situ FTIR experiments and theoretical calculations.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 2.2. Cyclic voltammetry experiments
text: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) experiments were performed through CHI electrochemical workstation (CHI760, China). A platinum rotating disk electrode (Pt-RDE) with a diameter of 5 mm, a platinum sheet and a Hg/ Hg _2S0_4 electrode (saturated K_2SO_4 solution, SMSE) were as the working electrode, counter electrode and reference electrode, respectively. The Pt-RDE was successively polished and ultrasonically cleaned before each experiment. The electrolyte composed of 220 g/L CuSO _4•5/H_2O_i, 49 g/L H_2SO_4 and 60 mg/L cl^- was defined as the virgin make-up solution (VMS).

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 2.3. In situ FTIR spectroscopy
text: In situ Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy experiments were carried out on an FTIR spectrometer equipped with a liquidnitrogen-cooling detector (Nicolet 8700, America). A thin-layer (~ 10 µm) electrolyte was pressed between the copper electrode and CaF _2 window. The spectra were recorded using the procedures of single potential alteration FTIR spectroscopy (SPAFTIRS) and multi-stepped FTIR (MSFTIR) [26]. The reference potential of the spectrum was − 0.4 V vs. SMSE electrode. The sample potentials of spectra were scanned from − 0.5 : to - 0.9 : V with a step potential of 0.1 V.

Based on the frontier molecular orbital theory, the energies of LUMO and HOMO are related to the electron-accepting and electron-donating abilities of molecules. A lower E _ LUMO means that the molecule possesses a higher tendency to receive electrons, and a higher E HOMO means that the molecule possesses a higher tendency to donate electrons [32].

text: It is very important to optimize the novel additive for TH copper void-free filling. In this work, we first successfully develop a novel SAbased acidic sulfate copper electronic plating process, and the process behaves the excellent copper void-free filling of TH. The complicated but effective molecule actions and synergistic effects among PEG, SPS and SA are carefully studied for the void-free filling of TH by CV, in situ FTIR experiments and theoretical calculations.

section: Insights into the synergistic effects of safranine in an acidic copper bath on through-hole void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection > 4. Conclusions
text: The complicated but effective molecule actions and synergistic effects among PEG, SPS and SA are carefully studied for the void-free filling of TH by CV, in situ FTIR experiments and theoretical calculations. This work is undoubtedly beneficial to understanding the interaction mechanisms of additives at a molecular level, and further developing and improving the acidic sulfate copper electronic plating in TH void-free filling.
